taxonomy.note: Kew accepts Yucca constricta. FNA provides an especially useful field character: the dry capsule is deeply constricted near the middle.

evidence: Hays — UT Plant Resources Center Flora of Purola Preserve lists Yucca constricta among naturally occurring, non-introduced plants of northern Hays County.
Travis — Balcones Canyonlands Preserve plant list for Travis County includes Buckley yucca (Yucca constricta).
Val Verde — Laughlin Air Force Base Integrated Natural Resources Management Plan, Del Rio/Val Verde County, lists Yucca constricta among observed woody plants.
target_zone_range.guardrail: County decision uses explicit county/local records alongside BONAP/NPSOT/Kew range context. No county is inferred from ecoregion membership alone.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the narrow straight leaves and the fruit: Buckley’s yucca makes low colonies of small rosettes with narrow whitish-threaded leaves, an unusually tall naked scape, and dry capsules pinched deeply at the middle.
diagnostic_traits: small to large open colonies, mostly acaulescent or with only a short stem
mostly straight linear leaves, usually about 0.7–1.5 cm wide
leaf margins whitish/light green and filiferous, shredding into threads
flowering stalk rises far above the leaves on a long naked scape
erect dry dehiscent capsule deeply constricted near the middle

confusers.separator: Y. constricta has narrow mostly straight white-threaded leaves and a deeply constricted capsule; Y. rupicola has broader flexible twisted leaves with orange/red denticulate margins.
Both have narrow filiferous leaves, but FNA separates Y. constricta by the deeply waist-constricted capsule; Y. tenuistyla capsules are not constricted and its leaves tend to recurve.
